english: Oh, it's you. Talk to Dozy, I'm going back to sleep.
french: Oh, c'est toi. Discute avec Dozy, je retourne me coucher.
russian: А, это ты. Обращайся к Дрёме, а я пойду дальше спать.
bulgarian: Oh, it's you. Talk to Dozy, I'm going back to sleep.

english: Hi, welcome to the Bathhouse...
french: Bonjour, bienvenue aux bains...
russian: Привет, добро пожаловать в купальню...
bulgarian: Hi, welcome to the Bathhouse...

english: Hey, [Ari]. Here for a bath?
french: Salut, [Ari]. Tu viens prendre un bain ?
russian:
Привет, [Ari].

Пришли

ПришлаПришёлПришло принять ванну?
bulgarian: Hey, [Ari]. Here for a bath?

english: Balor's the only person in town who can get me dried witchvine root, but he won't reveal his sources. It's vexing!
french: Ici, il n'y a que Balor qui puisse me fournir en racines de sorcerelierre séchées, mais il ne veut pas me dire où il les a. C'est vexant !
russian: Балор — единственный в городе, кто может достать сушёный корень ведьминой лозы, но свои источники он не раскрывает. Раздражает!
bulgarian: Balor's the only person in town who can get me dried witchvine root, but he won't reveal his sources. It's vexing!

english: Ah, hello.
french: Tiens, bonjour.
russian: А, привет.
bulgarian: Ah, hello.

english: So make up your mind or leave already.
french: Alors, tu te baignes ou tu déguerpis.
russian: Так что решайся или уходи.
bulgarian: So make up your mind or leave already.

english: Your bath awaits! I, however, do not.
french: Ton bain t'attendait ! Moi, pas vraiment.
russian: Ванна тебя ждёт! А вот я — нет.
bulgarian: Your bath awaits! I, however, do not.

english: The bathhouse was a bit empty after Elsie and Lady Adeline left... not that it bothers me one bit!
french: Les bains semblaient un peu vides quand Elsie et dame Adeline sont parties... et ça me va très bien comme ça.
russian: После отъезда Элси и леди Аделины в купальне стало пустовато... не то чтобы меня это хоть каплю волновало!
bulgarian: The bathhouse was a bit empty after Elsie and Lady Adeline left... not that it bothers me one bit!

english: Living inside a bathhouse has its perks, especially on days like today.
french: Par une journée comme celle-là, vivre dans un établissement de bains a ses avantages.
russian: Жить прямо в купальне — сплошные плюсы, особенно в такую погоду.
bulgarian: Living inside a bathhouse has its perks, especially on days like today.

english: The heat from the bath keeps the building nice and warm, no matter the time of year. Isn't that nice?
french: Toute l'année, le bâtiment est bien chauffé toute l'année, grâce à la vapeur des bains. C'est agréable, n'est-ce pas ?
russian: Жар от воды хорошо прогревает здание в любое время года. Приятно, правда?
bulgarian: The heat from the bath keeps the building nice and warm, no matter the time of year. Isn't that nice?

english: Maybe I'll get that new crystal ball I was eyeing...
french: Je vais peut-être craquer pour cette nouvelle boule de cristal qui me plaît tellement...
russian: Может, наконец, куплю тот хрустальный шар, на который давно заглядываюсь...
bulgarian: Maybe I'll get that new crystal ball I was eyeing...

english: The bathhouse gets busy in winter, which means the tesserae really piles up.
french: Les bains sont toujours pleins en hiver, et la caisse aussi.
russian: Зимой в купальне много народу — и тессеры накапливаются будь здоров.
bulgarian: The bathhouse gets busy in winter, which means the tesserae really piles up.

english: Thanks, me.
french: Même si c'est grâce à moi.
russian: Спасибо мне!
bulgarian: Thanks, me.

english: I suppose I should be thankful that business is good in the winter.
french: C'est une bonne chose que les affaires marchent bien en hiver.
russian: Думаю, стоит поблагодарить всех, кто поддерживает купальный бизнес зимой.
bulgarian: I suppose I should be thankful that business is good in the winter.

english: The biggest travesty about having to sit behind this desk all day is not being able to show off my boots.
french: L'inconvénient de rester assise toute la journée à la caisse, c'est de ne pas pouvoir montrer mes bottes.
russian: Когда весь день сидишь за стойкой, главная подстава — что некому показать мои шикарные сапоги.
bulgarian: The biggest travesty about having to sit behind this desk all day is not being able to show off my boots.

english: Ugh.
french: Argh.
russian: Фу.
bulgarian: Ugh.

english: I'll be thrilled when spring rolls around. The cold doesn't bother me, but the Bathhouse gets busy in winter, and that means I have to... you know... work.
french: Vivement le printemps ! Ce n'est pas que le froid me dérange, mais il y a plus de gens aux bains, et ça me donne plus de travail...
russian: Жду не дождусь, когда, наконец, придёт весна. Холода меня не смущают, но зимой в купальне всегда людно. А значит, мне надо... в общем... работать.
bulgarian: I'll be thrilled when spring rolls around. The cold doesn't bother me, but the Bathhouse gets busy in winter, and that means I have to... you know... work.

english: I'll have to speak with Celine if I'm going to make more extracts...
french: Je vais devoir en toucher deux mots à Céline si je veux en produire davantage...
russian: Надо будет попросить Селин принести ещё, ведь мне нужно делать экстракты...
bulgarian: I'll have to speak with Celine if I'm going to make more extracts...

english: Hm, am I out of the lavender oil already?
french: Hmm, je suis déjà à court d'huile de lavande ?
russian: Хм, неужели лавандовое масло уже кончилось?
bulgarian: Hm, am I out of the lavender oil already?

english: Practice, of course.
french: Tout est question d'entraînement, évidemment.
russian: Всё дело в сноровке.
bulgarian: Practice, of course.

english: Now you may be wondering, how does she keep her cape dry when she works in a bathhouse?
french: Tu te demandes peut-être comment je fais pour que ma cape reste sèche alors que je travaille aux bains.
russian: Тебя, возможно, волнует вопрос: как же ей удаётся не мочить плащ, работая в купальне?
bulgarian: Now you may be wondering, how does she keep her cape dry when she works in a bathhouse?

english: It's a great time to test new bath oils and herbal mixtures.
french: C'est une très bonne période pour tester de nouvelles huiles et de nouveaux onguents.
russian: Самое время тестировать новые масла и травяные смеси.
bulgarian: It's a great time to test new bath oils and herbal mixtures.

english: The bathhouse gets busy in the winter...
french: Il y a toujours du monde aux bains, en hiver...
russian: Зимой в купальне всегда много посетителей...
bulgarian: The bathhouse gets busy in the winter...

english: Your bath awaits. After you pay up, of course.
french: Ton bain est prêt. Mais passe d'abord à la caisse, je te prie.
russian: Ванна ждёт. После оплаты, разумеется.
bulgarian: Your bath awaits. After you pay up, of course.

english: Not that I care or anything.
french: Même si je m'en moque, dans le fond.
russian: Не то чтобы мне было важно.
bulgarian: Not that I care or anything.

english: If someone's in the bath too long, I send Dozy to check on them.
french: Si quelqu'un reste trop longtemps dans les bains, j'envoie Dozy voir si tout va bien.
russian: Если кто-то засиживается в ванне, я посылаю Дрёму проверить.
bulgarian: If someone's in the bath too long, I send Dozy to check on them.

english: Here for a bath? Tesserae goes on the counter, bath's on the right. You know the drill.
french: Tu viens te baigner ? Dépose tes tesserae sur le comptoir, les bains sont sur la droite. Tu sais comment ça se passe.
russian: На ванну? Тессеры на прилавок, купальня справа. Ты знаешь, как это работает.
bulgarian: Here for a bath? Tesserae goes on the counter, bath's on the right. You know the drill.

english: I looked like a raisin for the first month we got this place up and running.
french: J'étais ridée comme un pruneau le premier mois après l'ouverture.
russian: В первый месяц после открытия я была похожа на изюм.
bulgarian: I looked like a raisin for the first month we got this place up and running.

english: A sexy raisin, of course.
french: Un pruneau sexy, cela va sans dire.
russian: Но, конечно, весьма соблазнителный изюм!
bulgarian: A sexy raisin, of course.

english: The problem with running a bathhouse is that it's so easy to take one whenever you want.
french: Le problème quand on gère les bains, c'est qu'on a tendance à en prendre trop souvent.
russian: Когда управляешь купальней, появляется большая проблема: можно принимать ванну, когда захочешь.
bulgarian: The problem with running a bathhouse is that it's so easy to take one whenever you want.

english: I'm sure he'd like it if you gave it a try.
french: Je suis sûre qu'il aimerait que tu la testes.
russian: Он наверняка обрадуется, если ты попробуешь.
bulgarian: I'm sure he'd like it if you gave it a try.

english: Dozy did a good job with today's bath blend, [Ari].
french: Dozy a préparé une huile de bain vraiment agréable aujourd'hui, [Ari].
russian: Сегодня Дрёма приготовил отличную смесь для ванн, [Ari].
bulgarian: Dozy did a good job with today's bath blend, [Ari].

english: The snow got almost as tall as my thigh-highs.
french: La neige m'arrivait à mi-cuisses.
russian: Снега нападало почти до моих чулков.
bulgarian: The snow got almost as tall as my thigh-highs.

english: I remember my first winter in Mistria.
french: Je me souviens de mon premier hiver à Mistria.
russian: Я помню свою первую зиму в Мистрии.
bulgarian: I remember my first winter in Mistria.

english: Nobody comes to the Bathhouse in winter for a cold plunge.
french: L'hiver, on ne va pas aux bains pour se prélasser dans de l'eau fraîche.
russian: Окунуться в прорубь зимой можно и вне купальни.
bulgarian: Nobody comes to the Bathhouse in winter for a cold plunge.

english: Dozy, be a dear and check on the bath's temperature, would you?
french: Dozy, sois un amour et va vérifier la température des bains, veux-tu ?
russian: Дрёма, будь другом, сходи проверь температуру воды.
bulgarian: Dozy, be a dear and check on the bath's temperature, would you?

english: Of course it does.
french: Mais oui, quelle question !
russian: Конечно, идёт.
bulgarian: Of course it does.

english: Elsie said I should try putting my hair up for the Beach. What do you think, does it look good?
french: C'est Elsie qui m'a dit de m'attacher les cheveux quand je vais à la plage. Qu'en penses-tu ? Ça me va bien ?
russian: Элси сказала, что мне стоит забрать волосы наверх, если иду на пляж. Ну как, идёт?
bulgarian: Elsie said I should try putting my hair up for the Beach. What do you think, does it look good?

english: You're blocking my sun, [Ari].
french: Tu me caches le soleil, [Ari].
russian: Ты загораживаешь мне солнце, [Ari].
bulgarian: You're blocking my sun, [Ari].

english: Like a =Latte= isn't breakfast? Ridiculous.
french: Comme si un =café latte= ne suffisait pas comme petit-déjeuner... N'importe quoi.
russian: Как будто =латте= это не нормальный завтрак. Чушь.
bulgarian: Like a =Latte= isn't breakfast? Ridiculous.

english: Dozy made me get up to eat a proper breakfast at the Inn.
french: Dozy m'a obligée à me lever pour prendre un vrai petit-déjeuner à l'auberge.
russian: Дрёма заставил меня встать и позавтракать как положено — в трактире.
bulgarian: Dozy made me get up to eat a proper breakfast at the Inn.

english: Ah well. Happens to the best of us.
french: Enfin, cela arrive même aux meilleurs d'entre nous.
russian: Ну и ладно. Со всеми случается.
bulgarian: Ah well. Happens to the best of us.

english: Between you and me, I'm not really sure what I'm brewing anymore. I'd say this concoction is having a bit of an identity crisis.
french: Je t'avoue que je ne sais plus très bien ce que contient ce chaudron. Cette mixture traverse une crise d'identité.
russian: Между нами, я уже не уверена, что именно варю. Кажется, это зелье переживает личностный кризис.
bulgarian: Between you and me, I'm not really sure what I'm brewing anymore. I'd say this concoction is having a bit of an identity crisis.

english: Shh [Ari], I'm brainstorming a new potion... I have a big evening of brewing ahead of me.
french: Chuuut, [Ari], je réfléchis à une nouvelle potion... Je vais passer ma soirée à tester des mélanges.
russian: Тсс, [Ari], я обдумываю новое зелье... Вечером предстоит большая варка.
bulgarian: Shh [Ari], I'm brainstorming a new potion... I have a big evening of brewing ahead of me.

english: I followed the resonance there, but I lost track of it...
french: J'ai suivi la réverbération que j'avais ressentie jusqu'à là-bas, mais j'ai perdu sa trace...
russian: Я пошла по резонансу, но в какой-то момент потеряла его...
bulgarian: I followed the resonance there, but I lost track of it...

english: And then a mysterious, disembodied voice said "a little to the left".
french: Puis une mystérieuse voix désincarnée a dit : « Un petit peu plus à gauche. »
russian: А потом загадочный голос ниоткуда сказал: «чуть левее».
bulgarian: And then a mysterious, disembodied voice said "a little to the left".

english: I'm sure you were just hearing things.
french: Je crois que tu entends des voix.
russian: Наверное, просто послышалось.
bulgarian: I'm sure you were just hearing things.

english: Maybe it was a ghost...
french: C'était peut-être un fantôme...
russian: Может, это был призрак...
bulgarian: Maybe it was a ghost...

english: Y-yeah... I'm sure it was nothing...
french: O-Oui... C'était sûrement mon imagination...
russian: Д-да... наверное, ничего особенного...
bulgarian: Y-yeah... I'm sure it was nothing...

english: S-stop it [Ari]. Ghosts aren't real. Right?
french: A-Arrête un peu, [Ari]. Les fantômes n'existent pas, hein ?
russian: П-прекрати, [Ari]. Призраков не существует. Правда?
bulgarian: S-stop it [Ari]. Ghosts aren't real. Right?

english: There's been a strange vibration in Mistria's leylines since the path to the Deep Woods was cleared.
french: Je ressens une étrange vibration dans les alignements de Mistria, depuis que le chemin qui mène à Boissombre a été dégagé.
russian: С тех пор, как расчистили путь в Глубокую чащу, магические жилы Мистрии странно вибрируют.
bulgarian: There's been a strange vibration in Mistria's leylines since the path to the Deep Woods was cleared.

english: You wouldn't believe how long it takes to build up a proper patina.
french: Tu n'imagines pas le temps qu'il faut pour obtenir cette patine.
russian: Ты не поверишь, сколько времени уходит на правильную патину.
bulgarian: You wouldn't believe how long it takes to build up a proper patina.

english: This cauldron is one of the few things I brought with me to Mistria.
french: Mon chaudron est l'une des seules choses qui m'ont suivie à Mistria.
russian: Этот котёл — одна из немногих вещей, что я привезла с собой в Мистрию.
bulgarian: This cauldron is one of the few things I brought with me to Mistria.

english: It's bright and bubbling hot! What more warning could you need?
french: Un liquide qui bouillonne et dont la couleur est changeante ! Qu'est-ce qu'ils ne comprennent pas ?
russian: Оно же яркого цвета, кипит и пузырится! Неужели это недостаточно ясное предупреждение?
bulgarian: It's bright and bubbling hot! What more warning could you need?

english: Those children threw a stick into my cauldron! And then one of them was on the brink of putting their hand into this melange before I intervened.
french: Les gosses ont jeté une petite branche dans mon chaudron ! L'un d'eux allait plonger sa main dedans. Il a fallu que j'intervienne.
russian: Дети бросили в мой котёл палку! А одна чуть не засунула руку в варево. Хорошо, что я успела её отдёрнуть.
bulgarian: Those children threw a stick into my cauldron! And then one of them was on the brink of putting their hand into this melange before I intervened.

english: That Celine asks me some interesting questions about the properties of flowers, but she also seems to know more than I'd expect of a rural village girl.
french: Céline me pose des questions intéressantes sur les propriétés des fleurs, mais elle semble en savoir plus que ce qu'on attendrait d'une jeune fille de la campagne.
russian: Селин задаёт мне интересные вопросы о свойствах цветов, но при этом знает подозрительно много для деревенской девочки.
bulgarian: That Celine asks me some interesting questions about the properties of flowers, but she also seems to know more than I'd expect of a rural village girl.

english: I'd be curious to peek at this Codex Mistria she's always on about.
french: Je serais assez curieuse de jeter un œil à ce Codex Mistria auquel elle fait si souvent référence.
russian: Любопытно было бы взглянуть на этот её «Кодекс Мистрии».
bulgarian: I'd be curious to peek at this Codex Mistria she's always on about.

english: She must want something from me. What do you suppose she's getting at?
french: Elle attend sans doute quelque chose de moi. Qu'est-ce qu'elle me veut, à ton avis ?
russian: Наверняка ей от меня что-то нужно. Как думаешь, к чему она клонит?
bulgarian: She must want something from me. What do you suppose she's getting at?

english: Hm. I guess I may as well humor her.
french: Hmmm. Autant lui faire plaisir.
russian: Хм. Что ж, пожалуй, уважу её.
bulgarian: Hm. I guess I may as well humor her.

english: Celine invited me over for tea again...
french: Céline m'a encore invitée à venir boire le thé...
russian: Селин снова позвала меня на чай...
bulgarian: Celine invited me over for tea again...

english: Stop looking so chipper in the morning. You'll be a bad influence on Dozy.
french: Arrête tout cet entrain de bon matin. Tu as une mauvaise influence sur Dozy.
russian: Не светись так с утра. Ты плохо влияешь на Дрёму.
bulgarian: Stop looking so chipper in the morning. You'll be a bad influence on Dozy.

english: What's the point of helping people if you're only giving preventative advice? If I were Valen I'd be prescribing potions left and right!
french: On ne peut pas aider les gens en faisant uniquement de la prévention. À la place de Valen, je prescrirais des potions pour tout et n'importe quoi !
russian: Какой смысл помогать людям, если давать только профилактические советы? Будь я Вален, уже давно прописывала бы зелья направо и налево!
bulgarian: What's the point of helping people if you're only giving preventative advice? If I were Valen I'd be prescribing potions left and right!

english: Sigh... there's never anything good on. Maybe one of the girls left me a message...
french: Pfff... Il n'y a jamais rien d'intéressant à voir. Peut-être qu'une des filles m'a laissé un message ?
russian: *вздох*... Опять ничего стоящего не идёт. Может, кто-то из девочек оставил сообщение...
bulgarian: Sigh... there's never anything good on. Maybe one of the girls left me a message...

english: *yawn* I was up a bit late last night. These ley lines won't log themselves...
french: *bâillement* J'ai veillé très tard, la nuit dernière. Il faut bien que quelqu'un répertorie ces alignements...
russian: *зевает* Засиделась вчера допоздна. Магические жилы сами себя не опишут...
bulgarian: *yawn* I was up a bit late last night. These ley lines won't log themselves...

english: Adeline will make me fill out a ton of paperwork.
french: Adeline me forcerait à remplir des tas de paperasses.
russian: Аделина заставит меня оформлять кучу бумажек.
bulgarian: Adeline will make me fill out a ton of paperwork.

english: Welcome! If you soak in the bath, do me a favor and don't drown.
french: Bienvenue ! Si jamais tu prends un bain, merci de ne pas te noyer.
russian: Добро пожаловать! Если собираешься купаться — сделай одолжение, не утони.
bulgarian: Welcome! If you soak in the bath, do me a favor and don't drown.

english: Try not to drown. I'd prefer to keep you around.
french: Essaie de ne pas te noyer. Je préférerais te garder en vie.
russian:
Не утони, пожалуйста. Я бы хотела, чтобы ты

были целы

была целабыл целбыло цело.
bulgarian: Try not to drown. I'd prefer to keep you around.

english: Welcome! If you soak in the bath, do me a favor...
french: Bienvenue ! Si jamais tu prends un bain, rends-moi service...
russian: Добро пожаловать! Если будешь отмокать в ванне, сделай одолжение...
bulgarian: Welcome! If you soak in the bath, do me a favor...

english: Sticks, maybe?
french: Qu'on lui lance un bâton ?
russian: Наверное, палки...
bulgarian: Sticks, maybe?

english: Small business grants?
french: Qu'il monte sa petite entreprise ?
russian: Гранты для малого бизнеса?
bulgarian: Small business grants?

english: I wonder what Dozy dreams about.
french: À quoi peut bien rêver Dozy ?
russian: Интересно, что снится Дрёме.
bulgarian: I wonder what Dozy dreams about.

english: He's not sure he can pull it off, though.
french: Apparemment, il n'est pas sûr de pouvoir marcher avec...
russian: Он не уверен, что они ему пойдут.
bulgarian: He's not sure he can pull it off, though.

english: Dozy always makes me do the grocery shopping because he can't reach the top shelf! I keep telling him, that's what platform boots are for!
french: C'est toujours moi qui fais les courses pour Dozy parce qu'il n'arrive pas à atteindre les étagères du haut ! Je lui dis pourtant que c'est à ça que servent les talons hauts !
russian: Дрёма всегда отправляет меня за покупками, потому что не достаёт до верхней полки! Я всё говорю ему: для этого и придумали платформы!
bulgarian: Dozy always makes me do the grocery shopping because he can't reach the top shelf! I keep telling him, that's what platform boots are for!

english: Zzz... Dozy, be a dear and handle the counter...
french: Zzz... Dozy, sois gentil, occupe-toi du comptoir...
russian: *спит*... Дрёма, будь лапочкой, встань за стойку...
bulgarian: Zzz... Dozy, be a dear and handle the counter...

english: Let's keep it down. Dozy's had a long day.
french: Tâchons de ne pas faire de bruit. La journée a été longue pour Dozy.
russian: Потише, ладно? У Дрёмы был тяжёлый день.
bulgarian: Let's keep it down. Dozy's had a long day.

english: What am I, dead weight? I'll show her!
french: Et moi, je ne sers à rien ? Elle va voir !
russian: Она думает, я тут просто так сижу? Я ей покажу!
bulgarian: What am I, dead weight? I'll show her!

english: Valen said that Dozy could run this bathhouse by himself!
french: D'après Valen, Dozy pourrait gérer les bains à lui tout seul !
russian: Вален сказала, что Дрёма и сам бы мог управлять купальней!
bulgarian: Valen said that Dozy could run this bathhouse by himself!

english: I don't mind helping him with a translation now and then, but he'd better not push it...
french: Je veux bien lui traduire quelque chose une fois de temps en temps, mais que ça ne devienne pas une habitude...
russian: Я не против иногда помочь с переводом, но пусть не наглеет...
bulgarian: I don't mind helping him with a translation now and then, but he'd better not push it...

english: The pup, Eiland... he certainly has a penchant for asking questions, doesn't he?
french: Ce gamin, Eiland... Il aime bien poser tout un tas de questions, non ?
russian: Этот щенок Эйланд... уж больно любит задавать вопросы, да?
bulgarian: The pup, Eiland... he certainly has a penchant for asking questions, doesn't he?

english: I don't mind helping him with a translation now and then, but he'd better not push it...
french: Je veux bien lui traduire quelque chose une fois de temps en temps, mais que ça ne devienne pas une habitude...
russian: Я не против иногда помочь с переводом, но пусть не наглеет...
bulgarian: I don't mind helping him with a translation now and then, but he'd better not push it...

english: Those are a bit overwhelming, even for me.
french: L'odeur est un peu trop entêtante, même pour moi.
russian: Даже для меня это немного перебор.
bulgarian: Those are a bit overwhelming, even for me.

english: Let's see... Eiland's favorite bath oils are the ones that smell like cake.
french: Alors... Eiland préfère les huiles de bain qui sentent les pâtisseries.
russian: Посмотрим... Любимые масла Эйланда — те, что пахнут пирожными.
bulgarian: Let's see... Eiland's favorite bath oils are the ones that smell like cake.

english: But Valen's always asking about things like "efficacy" and "side effects." UGH.
french: Mais Valen me questionne toujours sur l'efficacité et les effets secondaires de mes remèdes. Quel culot !
russian: Но Вален всё время говорит то про «эффективность», то про «побочные эффекты». УФ.
bulgarian: But Valen's always asking about things like "efficacy" and "side effects." UGH.

english: I've heard Errol can't sleep. I've got a potion that'll knock him right out...
french: Il paraît qu'Errol a du mal à trouver le sommeil. J'ai une potion qui peut le mettre KO en un rien de temps...
russian: Слышала, Эррол не может уснуть. У меня есть зелье, которое вырубает на раз...
bulgarian: I've heard Errol can't sleep. I've got a potion that'll knock him right out...

english: Josephine seems to prefer floral scents for the bath. Those are the days she's here the most.
french: Joséphine préfère les bains aux senteurs florales. Elle vient beaucoup plus souvent ces jours-là.
russian: Джозефина, похоже, предпочитает цветочные ароматы. В такие дни она появляется чаще всего.
bulgarian: Josephine seems to prefer floral scents for the bath. Those are the days she's here the most.

english: It's not that I want to go tonight's gathering at the Inn. I'm simply doing this little hamlet a favor by showing up.
french: Ce n'est pas que je meure d'envie de retrouver les autres à l'auberge ce soir, mais il faut bien que je fasse profiter les habitants de ce trou perdu de ma présence.
russian: Я не то чтобы хочу идти сегодня в трактир. Я просто делаю этой деревушке одолжение своим присутствием.
bulgarian: It's not that I want to go tonight's gathering at the Inn. I'm simply doing this little hamlet a favor by showing up.

english: My cupboard is always stocked.
french: Mon armoire est toujours pleine.
russian: Мой шкафчик всегда полон.
bulgarian: My cupboard is always stocked.

english: Foraging is good in Mistria, isn't it? The soil supports all kinds of wild plants, throughout the seasons.
french: On trouve de nombreux produits dans la nature, à Mistria, hein ? Le sol offre une grande variété de plantes en toute saison.
russian: В Мистрии хорошо собирать травы, не так ли? Почва поддерживает всё дикорастущее почти круглый год.
bulgarian: Foraging is good in Mistria, isn't it? The soil supports all kinds of wild plants, throughout the seasons.

english: I can go out foraging twice as often as I could back home! Everything just grows right back.
french: Je peux aller cueillir des plantes sauvages deux fois plus souvent que là d'où je viens. Tout repousse en un rien de temps !
russian: Я могу собирать растения вдвое чаще, чем дома! Всё отрастает с какой-то дикой скоростью.
bulgarian: I can go out foraging twice as often as I could back home! Everything just grows right back.

english: Lend me your farmer's knowledge, [Ari]. Is there something special about the soil in Mistria?
french: Fais-moi profiter de tes connaissances en agriculture, [Ari]. La terre de Mistria a-t-elle quelque chose de spécial ?
russian: Поделись-ка со мной своей земледельческой мудростью, [Ari]. Есть что-то особенное в почве в Мистрии, да?
bulgarian: Lend me your farmer's knowledge, [Ari]. Is there something special about the soil in Mistria?

english: I never have enough =Nettle=!
french: Je n'ai jamais assez d'=orties= !
russian: У меня её вечно не хватает!
bulgarian: I never have enough =Nettle=!

english: I don't know why I'm milling around on the eastern road. It's =Nettle= that I need.
french: Je ne sais pas pourquoi je perds mon temps sur la route de l'est. Ce qu'il me faut, ce sont des =orties=.
russian: Не знаю, зачем я торчу на восточной дороге. Мне же нужна =крапива=.
bulgarian: I don't know why I'm milling around on the eastern road. It's =Nettle= that I need.

english: The foraging in Mistria is preternaturally good. The way this land renews itself... there's certainly something special about it.
french: Pouvoir obtenir tant de produits naturels aussi facilement est presque anormal. La terre se renouvelle d'elle-même... Il y a vraiment quelque chose de spécial, ici.
russian: Собирательство в Мистрии какое-то сверхъестественное. Эта земля сама себя обновляет... в ней точно что-то есть.
bulgarian: The foraging in Mistria is preternaturally good. The way this land renews itself... there's certainly something special about it.

english: Mistria has such a verdant countryside, foraging is always very rewarding.
french: La nature est si verdoyante à Mistria que la récolte est toujours bonne.
russian: В Мистрии такие зелёные просторы, что травы собирать — одно удовольствие.
bulgarian: Mistria has such a verdant countryside, foraging is always very rewarding.

english: When the going gets tough, the smart go to bed.
french: Il vaut parfois mieux remettre les choses au lendemain. La nuit porte conseil.
russian: «Когда становится трудно, умные идут спать».
bulgarian: When the going gets tough, the smart go to bed.

english: Ugh, I'm hung up on the formula for this mixture. What's that old saying?
french: Grrr, je bloque sur la formule de ce remède. Comment interpréter ce texte ancien ?
russian: Угх, застряла на формуле этого зелья. Как там говорится?..
bulgarian: Ugh, I'm hung up on the formula for this mixture. What's that old saying?

english: I appreciate the Inn's free soup, but I'd rather have some free wine.
french: J'aime bien la soupe gratuite de l'auberge, mais je préférerais qu'ils offrent du vin.
russian: Бесплатный суп в трактире — это, конечно, здорово, но я бы предпочла бесплатное вино.
bulgarian: I appreciate the Inn's free soup, but I'd rather have some free wine.

english: Rain, rain, go away... I could do it with a spell, but I'm so sleepy...
french: Toute cette pluie... Je pourrais lancer un sort pour qu'elle s'arrête, mais j'ai tellement sommeil...
russian: Дождик, уйди... Я могла бы развеять тебя заклинанием, но спать охота...
bulgarian: Rain, rain, go away... I could do it with a spell, but I'm so sleepy...

english: My coming here is number one, of course.
french: La première étant ma venue à moi, cela va de soi.
russian: Первое, разумеется, — мой приезд.
bulgarian: My coming here is number one, of course.

english: Elsie coming to Mistria is the second best thing to happen to this dinky backwater.
french: Le déménagement d'Elsie à Mistria est la deuxième meilleure chose qu'il soit arrivé à ce trou perdu.
russian: То, что Элси приехала в Мистрию, — второе лучшее, что случилось с этим захолустьем.
bulgarian: Elsie coming to Mistria is the second best thing to happen to this dinky backwater.

english: Please go rest... just looking at you is making me exhausted, and I deserve better.
french: Je t'en prie, va te reposer... Rien que de te voir t'activer, ça m'épuise, et je n'ai pas mérité ça.
russian: Пожалуйста, иди отдохни... На тебя даже смотреть утомительно, а я заслуживаю лучшего.
bulgarian: Please go rest... just looking at you is making me exhausted, and I deserve better.

english: Is that right? Well, [Ari], you can call me Juniper. I recently opened the one and only $Bathhouse$ in this backwater village.
french: C'est bien ça ? Eh bien, [Ari], tu peux m'appeler Juniper. J'ai ouvert il y a peu cet établissement de $bains$, le seul et unique de ce trou perdu.
russian: Вот как. Что ж, [Ari], зови меня Джунипер. Недавно я открыла первую и единственную $купальню$ в этой глуши.
bulgarian: Is that right? Well, [Ari], you can call me Juniper. I recently opened the one and only $Bathhouse$ in this backwater village.

english: What's a lady like you doing in a place like this?
french: Que peut bien faire ici une dame aussi raffinée ?
russian: Что такая особа, как ты, делает в месте вроде этого?
bulgarian: What's a lady like you doing in a place like this?

english: A backwater bathhouse, eh?
french: Des bains dans un trou perdu, tiens donc ?
russian: Купальня в глуши, значит?
bulgarian: A backwater bathhouse, eh?

english: Well, like you, I have my own reasons for being here.
french: Disons que, comme toi, j'ai mes raisons pour être ici.
russian: Ну, как и у тебя, у меня есть свои причины тут быть.
bulgarian: Well, like you, I have my own reasons for being here.

english: Aside from catering to the grubby townsfolk, I have my own reasons for being here...
french: Outre m'occuper de villageois crasseux, j'ai mes raisons pour être ici...
russian: Помимо того, что я обслуживаю грязноватых местных жителей, у меня есть и свои дела...
bulgarian: Aside from catering to the grubby townsfolk, I have my own reasons for being here...

english: Anyway, please stop in often. By the look of it, you could certainly use it.
french: Bref, passe me voir souvent. Ça ne te ferait pas mal, à ce que je vois.
russian: В любом случае, заглядывай почаще. Судя по виду, тебе это не помешает.
bulgarian: Anyway, please stop in often. By the look of it, you could certainly use it.

english: OH HO HO HO!
french: OH HO HO HO !
russian: О-ХО-ХО-ХО!
bulgarian: OH HO HO HO!

english: So you're the newcomer?
french: Alors c'est toi qui viens d'arriver au village ?
russian: Значит, это ты — новичок?
bulgarian: So you're the newcomer?

english: Thanks?
french: Euh... Merci ?
russian: Спасибо?
bulgarian: Thanks?

english: Oooh, him and that rude chicken of his!
french: Oooh, ne me parle pas de lui et de sa poule si vulgaire !
russian: Ооох, он и его грубая курица!
bulgarian: Oooh, him and that rude chicken of his!

english: The things she clucked about Dozy! You wouldn't believe it.
french: Elle a caqueté des choses sur Dozy que je n'oserais même pas répéter.
russian:
Ты бы

слышали

слышаласлышалслышало, что она кудахтала про Дрёму Просто уму непостижимо.
bulgarian: The things she clucked about Dozy! You wouldn't believe it.

english: You should feel honored, [Ari]. You're the first farmer I've deigned to be acceptable in my presence.
french: Tu es <he>le premier fermier</he><she>la première fermière</she><they>læ premier·ère fermier·ère</they> que je daigne honorer de ma présence. J'espère que tu en as conscience, [Ari].
russian:
[Ari], ты

первые фермеры

первая фермеркапервый фермерпервое фермер, чьё присутствие рядом с собой я готова терпеть. Можешь считать это честью для себя.
bulgarian: You should feel honored, [Ari]. You're the first farmer I've deigned to be acceptable in my presence.

english: And you're the first bathhouse owner I've made friends with!
french: Et toi, tu es la première propriétaire de bains avec qui je me lie d'amitié !
russian:
А ты — первая владельца купальни, с которой я

подружились

подружиласьподружилсяподружилось!
bulgarian: And you're the first bathhouse owner I've made friends with!

english: What about Hayden?
french: Et Hayden, alors ?
russian: А как же Хейден?
bulgarian: What about Hayden?

english: Even in a town as small as this, I'm sure you can find someone who will want to hear about your day that isn't me.
french: Même dans une ville aussi petite, je suis certaine que tu n'auras pas de mal à trouver quelqu'un d'autre qui sera ravi que tu lui racontes ta journée.
russian: В этой деревне точно найдётся кто-нибудь, кто захочет послушать, как прошёл твой день, вместо меня.
bulgarian: Even in a town as small as this, I'm sure you can find someone who will want to hear about your day that isn't me.

english: Please don't feel obligated to make small talk every time you see me.
french: Ne te sens pas obligé<he></he><she>e</she><they>·e</they> de papoter avec moi à chaque fois qu'on se croise.
russian:
Знаешь, ты не

обязаны

обязанаобязанобязано заводить со мной разговор при каждой встрече.
bulgarian: Please don't feel obligated to make small talk every time you see me.

english: Buy one bath, get one bath.
french: Pour un bain payé, tu peux prendre un bain.
russian: Платишь за одну ванну — получаешь одну ванну!
bulgarian: Buy one bath, get one bath.

english: Oh ho ho!
french: Ho ho ho !
russian: О-хо-хо!
bulgarian: Oh ho ho!

english: I'm offering a new resident discount you might want to take advantage of.
french: J'offre une remise pour les nouveaux arrivants, tu devrais en profiter.
russian: У нас скидка для новых жителей — можешь воспользоваться.
bulgarian: I'm offering a new resident discount you might want to take advantage of.

english: History can certainly teach us a lot, but it's also very pretty to look at.
french: L'histoire peut nous apprendre beaucoup de choses, mais on peut aussi contempler sa beauté.
russian: История может многому научить... Но кроме этого, история — это просто красиво.
bulgarian: History can certainly teach us a lot, but it's also very pretty to look at.

english: I thought Olric was a fool, but now I'm convinced there's cunning behind those eyes. No one could actually be such a simpleton... right?
french: Je prenais Olric pour un idiot, mais je suis désormais convaincue qu'il est plus malin qu'il n'y paraît. Personne ne peut être aussi stupide... non ?
russian: Я думала, Ольрик — дурак, но теперь уверена, что за этими глазами прячется хитрость. Ну не может же кто-то быть настолько простым... правда?
bulgarian: I thought Olric was a fool, but now I'm convinced there's cunning behind those eyes. No one could actually be such a simpleton... right?

english: I think I make Hayden nervous... Maybe he's wiser than he looks.
french: J'ai l'impression que je rends Hayden nerveux... Il est peut-être plus intelligent qu'il n'y paraît.
russian: Кажется, я пугаю Хейдена... Может, он умнее, чем кажется.
bulgarian: I think I make Hayden nervous... Maybe he's wiser than he looks.

english: And to avoid making the same mistakes of the poor souls who came before us.
french: Et d'éviter de répéter les erreurs commises par les pauvres âmes qui nous ont précédées.
russian: И помогает не повторить ошибки бедняг, что были до нас.
bulgarian: And to avoid making the same mistakes of the poor souls who came before us.

english: Knowing the past is important to a sorceress. It helps fill out our own secret histories.
french: Pour une sorcière, bien connaître le passé est primordial. Cela nous permet de mieux comprendre les secrets de notre histoire commune.
russian: Знать прошлое — важно для чародейки. Оно дополняет нашу личную тайную историю.
bulgarian: Knowing the past is important to a sorceress. It helps fill out our own secret histories.

english: Hm? You don't have to wake me up... leave the money on the table and enjoy the bath... let a girl sleep...
french: Mmm ? Pas la peine de me réveiller, laisse juste l'argent sur le comptoir et va profiter des bains... Laisse-moi dormir...
russian: Хм? Можешь не будить меня... Оставь деньги на столе и наслаждайся ванной... дай девочке поспать...
bulgarian: Hm? You don't have to wake me up... leave the money on the table and enjoy the bath... let a girl sleep...

english: Mistria is riddled with leylines of power... if I can map them all, I can harness them for... well. Don't worry your pretty little head about all that.
french: Il y a de nombreux alignements très puissants à Mistria... Si je parviens à tous les répertorier, j'utiliserai leur pouvoir pour... Non, rien. Ne te préoccupe pas de ça.
russian: Мистрию пронизывают магические жилы... Если я смогу их все нанести на карту, то смогу направить их на... Впрочем, не забивай свою милую головку.
bulgarian: Mistria is riddled with leylines of power... if I can map them all, I can harness them for... well. Don't worry your pretty little head about all that.

english: Today was a working Sunday... I'm ready to zone out in front of the crystal ball.
french: J'ai passé mon dimanche à travailler. Je n'ai qu'une envie, c'est de me vider la tête devant ma boule de cristal...
russian: Сегодня было рабочее воскресенье... Хочу просто залипнуть в хрустальный шар.
bulgarian: Today was a working Sunday... I'm ready to zone out in front of the crystal ball.

english: There's something so magical about music.
french: La musique a vraiment quelque chose de magique.
russian: В музыке есть нечто по-настоящему магическое.
bulgarian: There's something so magical about music.

english: I'm not much of a romantic, but I'm beginning to see why Elsie loves this garden so much.
french: Je ne suis pas du genre romantique, mais je commence à comprendre pourquoi Elsie aime tellement ce jardin.
russian: Я не очень склонна к романтике, но начинаю понимать, почему Элси без ума от этого сада.
bulgarian: I'm not much of a romantic, but I'm beginning to see why Elsie loves this garden so much.

english: They look different than the fish Terithia's always reeling in from the river.
french: Ils ont l'air différents de ceux que Terithia pêche habituellement dans la rivière.
russian: Они выглядят совсем не так, как те, что Теризия вечно таскает из реки.
bulgarian: They look different than the fish Terithia's always reeling in from the river.

english: I came out here to investigate a fluctuating leyline, but I ended up watching the fish in the manor pond instead.
french: Je suis venue trouver la cause des fluctuations d'un alignement, mais je suis restée à observer les poissons dans l'étang du manoir.
russian: Я вышла проверить колебания магических жил, а в итоге просто смотрела на рыб в пруду у особняка.
bulgarian: I came out here to investigate a fluctuating leyline, but I ended up watching the fish in the manor pond instead.

english: The loud one, March? He's actually quite skilled at his metalwork, when he's quiet enough to concentrate. Which doesn't happen nearly often enough.
french: March, c'est celui qui parle fort ? Il est bon forgeron, quand il arrive à la fermer assez longtemps pour se concentrer. Malheureusement, ça n'arrive pas souvent.
russian: Балабол этот Март, правда? А ведь в тишине он неплохо кует — только вот тишины от него не дождёшься.
bulgarian: The loud one, March? He's actually quite skilled at his metalwork, when he's quiet enough to concentrate. Which doesn't happen nearly often enough.

english: Go on [Ari], there's really nothing like a soak on a rainy day!
french: Allez, [Ari] ! Rien ne vaut un bon bain un jour de pluie.
russian: Вперёд, [Ari], ничто так не радует в дождь, как горячая ванна!
bulgarian: Go on [Ari], there's really nothing like a soak on a rainy day!

english: =Middlemist= flowers have such a wonderful scent, which I've infused into today's bath.
french: L'odeur des =camélias vaporeux= est sensationnelle, c'est avec ça que j'ai parfumé les bains aujourd'hui.
russian: Цветы =миддлемиста= так прекрасно пахнут — я добавила их в сегодняшнюю ванну.
bulgarian: =Middlemist= flowers have such a wonderful scent, which I've infused into today's bath.

english: Mulled wine on a rainy day... this little village gets some things right.
french: Un bon vin chaud un jour de pluie... Ils ont au moins compris certaines choses qu'ils ont bien comprises, dans ce village.
russian: Глинтвейн в дождливый день... кое-что эта деревенька всё-таки умеет.
bulgarian: Mulled wine on a rainy day... this little village gets some things right.

english: What's better than mulled wine after coming in from the cold?
french: Rien ne vaut un bon vin chaud quand on a eu froid, hein ?
russian: Что может быть лучше, чем глинтвейн после холодной улицы?
bulgarian: What's better than mulled wine after coming in from the cold?

english: The Inn does a great mulled wine in the winter.
french: Ils servent un excellent vin chaud à l'auberge en hiver.
russian: Зимой в трактире делают вкусный глинтвейн.
bulgarian: The Inn does a great mulled wine in the winter.

english: Eiland and Errol have certainly made my life easier, gathering them all in one place like this.
french: Eiland et Errol m'ont sacrément facilité la vie en les regroupant toutes en un même endroit.
russian: Эйланд с Эрролом сильно упростили мне жизнь, собрав всё в одном месте.
bulgarian: Eiland and Errol have certainly made my life easier, gathering them all in one place like this.

english: The concentration of ancient relics in Mistria is an endless source of fascination.
french: Le nombre de reliques antiques qu'on trouve à Mistria n'a de cesse de me fasciner.
russian: Концентрация древних реликвий в Мистрии — бесконечный источник любопытства.
bulgarian: The concentration of ancient relics in Mistria is an endless source of fascination.

english: I wonder what archaeologists of the distant future will think when they find me buried with all my shoes.
french: Je me demande ce que les archéologues du futur penseront en me retrouvant enterrée avec toutes mes paires de chaussures.
russian: Интересно, что подумают археологи будущего, когда найдут меня, похороненную вместе со всей моей обувью.
bulgarian: I wonder what archaeologists of the distant future will think when they find me buried with all my shoes.

english: [Ari], I've got a new potion in the works, but I'm still balancing the formula... what do you think, less =Newt= or more =Newt=?
french: [Ari], je travaille à une nouvelle potion, mais je n'ai pas encore trouvé l'équilibre parfait pour la formule... Tu rajouterais des =tritons= à ma place ?
russian: [Ari], я работаю над новым зельем, но ещё подбираю формулу... как думаешь, меньше =тритонов= или больше =тритонов=?
bulgarian: [Ari], I've got a new potion in the works, but I'm still balancing the formula... what do you think, less =Newt= or more =Newt=?

english: There's new power here, deep beneath us. The earthquake must have revealed it.
french: Je ressens une nouvelle force très profondément enfouie sous nos pieds. Elle est sans doute apparue après le tremblement de terre.
russian: Здесь появилась новая сила, в самой глубине. Землетрясение, видимо, её открыло.
bulgarian: There's new power here, deep beneath us. The earthquake must have revealed it.

english: The Inn has a new vintage in, and it's splendid.
french: L'auberge a reçu un nouveau vin. C'est un régal.
russian: В трактире появилось новое вино — и оно великолепно.
bulgarian: The Inn has a new vintage in, and it's splendid.

english: Leave a girl to her late night concocting, would you?
french: Tu pourrais me laisser travailler sur mes mélanges ?
russian: Позволь ведьме спокойно повариться в своих ночных зельях, ладно?
bulgarian: Leave a girl to her late night concocting, would you?

english: A moment, [Ari]. I'm in contemplation of my orb.
french: Donne-moi un moment, [Ari]. Je contemple mon orbe.
russian: Минутку, [Ari]. Я в созерцании шара.
bulgarian: A moment, [Ari]. I'm in contemplation of my orb.

english: Can we chat another time, [Ari]? It's just getting to the good part.
french: Tu peux repasser une autre fois, [Ari] ? Le meilleur moment est sur le point de commencer.
russian: Давай поболтаем позже, [Ari]? Сейчас начинается самое интересное.
bulgarian: Can we chat another time, [Ari]? It's just getting to the good part.

english: This orb has so many channels, and yet there's nothing interesting on any of them!
french: Cet orbe a des tas de chaînes, mais il n'y a rien d'intéressant sur aucune d'elles !
russian: Столько каналов в этом кристалле — и ни один не показывает что-то стоящее!
bulgarian: This orb has so many channels, and yet there's nothing interesting on any of them!

english: Sigh. I can view untold dimensions with this orb, and not one of them is showing anything interesting.
french: *soupir* Je peux recevoir un nombre incalculable de dimensions à travers cet orbe, mais il n'y a rien d'intéressant dans aucune d'elles.
russian: Эх. Я могу видеть бесконечные измерения... и ни в одном ничего интересного.
bulgarian: Sigh. I can view untold dimensions with this orb, and not one of them is showing anything interesting.

english: Suddenly it's four hours later, you've eaten an entire bag of =Water Chestnut Fritters=, and you're wondering what happened to your life.
french: Sans rien voir, quatre heures se sont écoulées, tu as vidé un sachet entier de =châtaignes d'eau grillées= et tu te demandes ce qui t'est arrivé.
russian: Вдруг прошло четыре часа, весь пакет =жареных водяных орешков= съеден, и ты не понимаешь, как докатилась до такой жизни.
bulgarian: Suddenly it's four hours later, you've eaten an entire bag of =Water Chestnut Fritters=, and you're wondering what happened to your life.

english: The thing about scrying at the crystal ball is you sit down to do one thing, and then you're stuck there.
french: Le problème avec une boule de cristal, c'est que tu veux vérifier un truc à venir, mais que tu te retrouves vite happé.
russian: Вот с этим шаром всегда так: садишься на минутку, а потом застреваешь.
bulgarian: The thing about scrying at the crystal ball is you sit down to do one thing, and then you're stuck there.

english: Curious.
french: Voilà qui est curieux.
russian: Любопытно.
bulgarian: Curious.

english: Many of the leylines I've discovered seem to converge on the Narrows. And the Mines, I suspect.
french: La plupart des alignements que j'ai découverts semblent converger vers les Terrasses. Et d'après mes calculs, vers les mines.
russian: Многие из найденных мной магических жил сходятся в Ущелье. И, подозреваю, в шахтах.
bulgarian: Many of the leylines I've discovered seem to converge on the Narrows. And the Mines, I suspect.

english: Shush, I finally got a clear signal.
french: Chut, la réception est bonne. Enfin !
russian: Тихо, я наконец-то поймала чёткий сигнал.
bulgarian: Shush, I finally got a clear signal.

english: You can stay, but you have to be quiet. My show is just starting to get good.
french: Tu peux rester, mais ne fais pas de bruit. C'est le passage de l'émission que je préfère.
russian: Можешь остаться, но помолчи. У меня тут шоу намечается.
bulgarian: You can stay, but you have to be quiet. My show is just starting to get good.

english: Finally... "42 Silly Labrador Pictures That Had Me On The Floor Laughing".
french: Il était temps... « 42 images trop drôles de labradors qui vous feront mourir de rire ».
russian: Наконец-то... «42 картинки смешных лабрадоров, от которых я каталась по полу от смеха».
bulgarian: Finally... "42 Silly Labrador Pictures That Had Me On The Floor Laughing".

english: The mist inside my crystal ball is clearing... the images are revealing themselves...
french: La brume de ma boule de cristal se dissipe et les images commencent enfin à apparaître...
russian: Туман в моём кристалле рассеивается... образы проявляются...
bulgarian: The mist inside my crystal ball is clearing... the images are revealing themselves...

english: It's important to plan tomorrow's shoes today.
french: Il faut prévoir dès aujourd'hui les chaussures qu'on portera demain.
russian: Планировать завтрашнюю обувь нужно сегодня.
bulgarian: It's important to plan tomorrow's shoes today.

english: Now, let's see what tomorrow's weather is...
french: Alors, que nous réserve la météo de demain ?
russian: Так, посмотрим, какая погода завтра...
bulgarian: Now, let's see what tomorrow's weather is...

english: Well? Don't keep him waiting.
french: Non ? Qu'est-ce que tu attends ?
russian: Ну? Не заставляй его ждать.
bulgarian: Well? Don't keep him waiting.

english: Have you pet Dozy today?
french: Tu as fait sa papouille quotidienne à Dozy, aujourd'hui ?
russian:
Ты сегодня уже

погладили

погладилапогладилпогладило Дрёму?
bulgarian: Have you pet Dozy today?

english: You want to know why I have chocolate?
french: Tu veux savoir pourquoi le chocolat en fait partie ?
russian: Хочешь знать, зачем мне шоколад?
bulgarian: You want to know why I have chocolate?

english: Chocolate's got many magical properties! Too many to list, in fact... well, I'll be on my way!
french: Il possède de nombreuses propriétés magiques ! Il y en a trop pour que je les énumère toutes... Bon, je suis très occupée !
russian: Шоколад обладает множеством магических свойств! Их слишком много, чтобы перечислять... так что я побежала!
bulgarian: Chocolate's got many magical properties! Too many to list, in fact... well, I'll be on my way!

english: I'm just collecting some reagents.
french: Je suis juste en train de rassembler des réactifs.
russian: Я просто собираю реагенты.
bulgarian: I'm just collecting some reagents.

english: Ahem. Sorry. Dozy says I should stop antagonizing customers.
french: Hum. Désolée. Dozy n'arrête pas de me dire que je dois arrêter de me mettre les clients à dos.
russian: Кхм. Прошу прощения. Дрёма говорит, мне стоит быть с клиентами поприветливее.
bulgarian: Ahem. Sorry. Dozy says I should stop antagonizing customers.

english: Oh, you want to take a bath while I watch the register? What if I want to take a bath while you watch the register?
french: Oh, tu veux prendre un bain pendant que je m'occupe de la caisse ? Et pourquoi pas le contraire au juste ?
russian: А, ты хочешь в ванну, пока я за стойкой? А если я пойду в ванну, а ты постоишь за стойкой?
bulgarian: Oh, you want to take a bath while I watch the register? What if I want to take a bath while you watch the register?

english: Do enjoy the bath. It's quite normal, I assure you.
french: Profite bien des bains. C'est normal, je peux te l'assurer.
russian: Приятного купания. Всё абсолютно нормально, честное слово.
bulgarian: Do enjoy the bath. It's quite normal, I assure you.

english: But I don't have to like it!
french: Ça ne veut pas dire que j'aime ça !
russian: Но это не значит, что мне это нравится!
bulgarian: But I don't have to like it!

english: Dozy says it's my shift, so here I am.
french: Dozy m'a dit que c'est à moi de tenir la caisse, donc me voilà.
russian: Дрёма говорит, сегодня моя смена, вот я и тут.
bulgarian: Dozy says it's my shift, so here I am.

english: It's important.
french: C'est important.
russian: Это важно.
bulgarian: It's important.

english: Don't forget to pay tribute to Dozy.
french: N'oublie pas de dire bonjour à Dozy.
russian: Не забудь навестить Дрёму.
bulgarian: Don't forget to pay tribute to Dozy.

english: I shouldn't have stayed up so late looking at my crystal ball... ugh.
french: Je n'aurais pas dû rester devant ma boule de cristal aussi tard... Oooh.
russian: Не стоило мне так долго пялиться в кристальный шар... уф.
bulgarian: I shouldn't have stayed up so late looking at my crystal ball... ugh.

english: Well, the bath's hot, and the lotion is complimentary.
french: Eh bien, le bain est chaud et la lotion est offerte.
russian: Что ж, ванна нагрета, крем прилагается бесплатно.
bulgarian: Well, the bath's hot, and the lotion is complimentary.

english: You're looking a bit chapped from the cold.
french: On dirait que le froid t'a provoqué des gerçures.
russian:
Ты, кажется,

обветрились

обветриласьобветрилсяобветрилось на морозе.
bulgarian: You're looking a bit chapped from the cold.

english: Reina's cooking is delicious... there MUST be a magical component to it, but she says it's all natural.
french: Tout ce que prépare Reina est délicieux... Je suis sûre qu'elle utilise un ingrédient magique, mais elle prétend que tout est naturel.
russian: Готовка Рейны — просто объедение... там ДОЛЖНА быть магия, но она клянётся, что всё натуральное.
bulgarian: Reina's cooking is delicious... there MUST be a magical component to it, but she says it's all natural.

english: Well well well, if it isn't my favorite... [Ari]. Today's bath oil is rosewater, in case you were wondering.
french: Tiens, tiens, voilà [Ari], <he>mon client préféré</he><she>ma cliente préférée</she><they>man client·e préféré·e</they>. Aujourd'hui, l'eau des bains est parfumée à l'huile de rose, si jamais tu te posais la question.
russian:
Вот так-так, это же

мои любимые

моя люимаямой любимыймоё любимое... [Ari]. Сегодняшнее масло для ванны — розовая вода, если вдруг интересно.
bulgarian: Well well well, if it isn't my favorite... [Ari]. Today's bath oil is rosewater, in case you were wondering.

english: I should really step up my game.
french: Je ferais bien de passer à la vitesse supérieure.
russian: Пора бы и мне взяться за дело.
bulgarian: I should really step up my game.

english: Sometimes I think about how the Ancient Witch Queens were already ruling all the realms when they were my age...
french: Parfois, je me rappelle qu'à mon âge, les Reines-sorcières d'antan régnaient déjà sur l'ensemble des royaumes...
russian: Иногда думаю: вот древние королевы-ведьмы уже правили царствами в моём возрасте...
bulgarian: Sometimes I think about how the Ancient Witch Queens were already ruling all the realms when they were my age...

english: The quiet one, Ryis? He helped me get this old bathhouse up and running again... he makes light of it, but I'm in his debt.
french: Ryis ? Celui qui n'est pas très loquace ? Il m'a aidée à rénover les anciens bains... Il fait comme si de rien n'était, mais je lui dois une fière chandelle.
russian: Тихоня Риз? Он помог мне восстановить эту старую купальню... делает вид, что ничего особенного, но я ему очень обязана.
bulgarian: The quiet one, Ryis? He helped me get this old bathhouse up and running again... he makes light of it, but I'm in his debt.

english: Seridia is asking me to find her a pair of platform heels.
french: Seridia m'a demandé de lui trouver une paire de chaussures à talons.
russian: Серидия попросила меня найти пару туфель с платформами.
bulgarian: Seridia is asking me to find her a pair of platform heels.

english: Could you please... gently... inform her there's no such thing as a high heel for dragons?
french: Tu pourrais lui dire... gentiment... que ça n'existe pas, les talons hauts pour les dragons ?
russian: Можешь, пожалуйста... аккуратно... донести до неё, что для драконов каблуков не придумали?
bulgarian: Could you please... gently... inform her there's no such thing as a high heel for dragons?

english: But [Ari].
french: Mais [Ari].
russian: Но, [Ari].
bulgarian: But [Ari].

english: If you see her trying to do her laundry in the Bathhouse again...
french: Si jamais tu la vois en train d'essayer à nouveau de faire sa lessive dans les bains...
russian: Если ты заметишь, что она приходит в купальню постирать вещи...
bulgarian: If you see her trying to do her laundry in the Bathhouse again...

english: Kindly dissuade her.
french: Essaie de l'en dissuader poliment.
russian: Попробуй её отсторожно отговорить.
bulgarian: Kindly dissuade her.

english: I know Seridia's the reborn Witch Queen and the origin of modern magic, so I don't feel like I can deny her much.
french: Je sais que Seridia est la Reine-sorcière revenue à la vie et qu'on lui doit la magie moderne, alors je ne peux sûrement rien lui refuser.
russian: Я знаю, что Серидия — новое воплощение королевы-ведьмы и прародительница всей современной магии. Так что мне не очень хочется ей отказывать.
bulgarian: I know Seridia's the reborn Witch Queen and the origin of modern magic, so I don't feel like I can deny her much.

english: Dozy says I should eat more vegetables, so here I am.
french: D'après Dozy, je devrais manger plus de légumes. C'est pour ça que je suis là.
russian: Дрёма говорит, мне стоит есть больше овощей, вот я и пришла.
bulgarian: Dozy says I should eat more vegetables, so here I am.

english: I ran out of... well, everything. So here I am.
french: Je suis à court de... De tout, en fait. C'est pour ça que je suis venue.
russian: У меня всё закончилось... буквально всё. Вот я и пришла.
bulgarian: I ran out of... well, everything. So here I am.

english: I left my grocery list at home. Again.
french: Une fois de plus, j'ai oublié ma liste de courses à la maison.
russian: Я снова забыла список покупок дома.
bulgarian: I left my grocery list at home. Again.

english: You didn't see me buying all this junk food. In fact, I was never here.
french: Ne dis à personne que j'ai acheté toutes ces cochonneries. Tu ne m'as pas vue ici.
russian:
Нет, ты не

видели

виделавиделвидело меня здесь, покупающей всю эту вредную еду. На самом деле меня тут и не было никогда.
bulgarian: You didn't see me buying all this junk food. In fact, I was never here.

english: Good quality, and they stay upright even when one of my potions explodes.
french: C'est de la qualité et elles ne tombent pas même si une de mes potions explose.
russian: Качество хорошее: выдерживают, даже когда мои зелья взрываются.
bulgarian: Good quality, and they stay upright even when one of my potions explodes.

english: Which is very rarely, mind you.
french: Ce qui n'arrive que très rarement, évidemment.
russian: Что происходит очень редко, если что.
bulgarian: Which is very rarely, mind you.

english: I commissioned Ryis and Landen to make me some shelves after I saw them at the General Store.
french: J'ai demandé à Ryis et à Landen de me fabriquer les mêmes étagères que celles du magasin général.
russian: Я заказала у Риза и Ландена новые полки, когда увидела те в лавке.
bulgarian: I commissioned Ryis and Landen to make me some shelves after I saw them at the General Store.

english: He scolds me if I load up on too much junk food...
french: Il me gronde si j'ai noté trop de cochonneries...
russian: Если я набираю слишком много нездоровой еды, он меня ругает.
bulgarian: He scolds me if I load up on too much junk food...

english: I always run my grocery list by Dozy.
french: Dozy vérifie toujours ma liste de courses.
russian: Я всегда показываю Дрёме свой список покупок.
bulgarian: I always run my grocery list by Dozy.

english: I was just wishing I could conjure my groceries at home, rather than trudging all the way out here.
french: J'imaginais lancer un sort de téléportation sur les courses, plutôt que de devoir les traîner depuis le magasin.
russian: Я бы хотела, чтобы еду можно было сотворить у себя дома, а не таскаться сюда каждый раз.
bulgarian: I was just wishing I could conjure my groceries at home, rather than trudging all the way out here.

english: Oh, don't mind me.
french: Oh, ne fais pas attention à moi.
russian: Не обращай на меня внимания.
bulgarian: Oh, don't mind me.

english: I can't be the only one in town looking for =Monster Powder=, can I? Why, I'd consider it a staple!
french: Je ne suis quand même pas la seule en ville à me servir de =poudre de monstre= ? Pour moi, c'est un ingrédient de base !
russian: Не может такого быть, что никому во всём городе, кроме меня, не нужна =пыль монстра=! По-моему, это товар первой необходимости!
bulgarian: I can't be the only one in town looking for =Monster Powder=, can I? Why, I'd consider it a staple!

english: The General Store is useful, but they never have everything I need.
french: Le magasin général est pratique, mais ils n'ont jamais tout ce dont j'ai besoin.
russian: Универмаг — это, конечно, полезно, но там никогда нет того, что мне нужно.
bulgarian: The General Store is useful, but they never have everything I need.

english: She's revealed herself to be quite knowledgeable. I respect that.
french: Elle a démontré qu'elle maîtrisait très bien son sujet. Je lui tire mon chapeau.
russian: Оказалось, она отлично разбирается в этом деле. Это достойно уважения.
bulgarian: She's revealed herself to be quite knowledgeable. I respect that.

english: I was talking to Celine about the best places to forage this and that.
french: Je discutais avec Céline des meilleurs endroits pour la cueillette de certaines plantes.
russian: Я расспрашивала Селин, где лучше собирать разные травы.
bulgarian: I was talking to Celine about the best places to forage this and that.

english: I've got a bathhouse to run!
french: J'ai des bains à gérer, moi !
russian: У меня вообще-то купальня на мне держится!
bulgarian: I've got a bathhouse to run!

english: Valen can't keep me under observation for a sniffle.
french: Valen ne peut pas me garder en observation à cause d'un tout petit rhume.
russian: У меня всего лишь насморк, Вален не стоит меня из-за него наблюдать.
bulgarian: Valen can't keep me under observation for a sniffle.

english: I might bring some home for Dozy, actually.
french: Je vais peut-être en rapporter à Dozy.
russian: Может, возьму немного домой для Дрёмы.
bulgarian: I might bring some home for Dozy, actually.

english: The soup today was quite good.
french: J'ai bien aimé la soupe du jour.
russian: Сегодняшний суп был на удивление хорош.
bulgarian: The soup today was quite good.

english: Reina's cooking is an alchemy all its own. I can't believe she's just giving it away for free!
french: La cuisine de Reina n'est pas sans rappeler l'alchimie. Quand je pense qu'elle offre tout ça gratuitement !
russian: Блюда Рейны — это какая-то особенная алхимия. Даже не верится, что она делится ими бесплатно!
bulgarian: Reina's cooking is an alchemy all its own. I can't believe she's just giving it away for free!

english: Today's soup smells positively delicious.
french: La soupe du jour sent délicieusement bon.
russian: Суп сегодня пахнет совершенно восхитительно.
bulgarian: Today's soup smells positively delicious.

english: Well, whatever they're doing, it's working. Cheers.
french: Je ne sais pas d'où il vient, mais il est très bon. Santé !
russian: Что бы они там ни делали, это работает. За здоровье.
bulgarian: Well, whatever they're doing, it's working. Cheers.

english: Hemlock says that Balor sources the wine for the Inn these days.
french: D'après Hemlock, c'est Balor qui approvisionne l'auberge en vin, ces temps-ci.
russian: Хемлок говорит, что теперь Балор поставляет вино для трактира.
bulgarian: Hemlock says that Balor sources the wine for the Inn these days.

english: This stele was built after the reign of the Witch Queens... I wonder what they would make of it.
french: Cette stèle a été érigée après le règne des Reines-sorcières... Je me demande ce qu'elles en penseraient.
russian: Эта стела была построена уже после Эпохи королев-ведьм... Интересно, что бы они о ней подумали.
bulgarian: This stele was built after the reign of the Witch Queens... I wonder what they would make of it.

english: This stele has a unique resonance, but that's about all I've been able to puzzle out.
french: Cette stèle a une résonance qui lui est propre, mais c'est la seule chose que j'ai pu déceler.
russian: У этой стелы особая аура, но больше ничего я в ней пока не разгадала.
bulgarian: This stele has a unique resonance, but that's about all I've been able to puzzle out.

english: Was something hidden here?
french: Il y avait quelque chose de caché là-dedans ?
russian: Там было что-то запрятано?
bulgarian: Was something hidden here?

english: Hm. The surface is utterly seamless, but I sense this stele has a sealed compartment.
french: Mmm. La surface est bien lisse, mais je sens qu'il y a compartiment caché sur cette stèle.

bulgarian: Tribute? For me? You shouldn't have.

russian: Спасибо, [Ari]. Я запрячу его для особого случая.

bulgarian: The Witch Queens used to dry and crush =Middlemist's= petals to paint their lips vivid crimson.

english: Oh ho ho ho!
french: Oh ho ho ho !
russian: О-хо-хо-хо!
bulgarian: Oh ho ho ho!

english: =Monster Powder=? Oh, I've got plans for this.
french: De la =poudre de monstre= ? Oh, je sais déjà comment je vais l'utiliser.
russian: =Пыль монстра=? О, на неё у меня давно планы.
bulgarian: =Monster Powder=? Oh, I've got plans for this.

english: Oh, I adore =Moon Fruit Cake=! That burst of flavor when you bite into a piece of moon fruit, it's like magic.
french: Oh, j'adore le =gâteau à la lunarine= ! Cette explosion de saveurs quand on croque un morceau de lunarine, c'est magique.
russian: О, я просто обожаю =торт из лунных ягод=! Когда попадается кусочек ягоды — это такой всплеск вкуса. Просто магия.
bulgarian: Oh, I adore =Moon Fruit Cake=! That burst of flavor when you bite into a piece of moon fruit, it's like magic.

english: How fun! Cheers, [Ari].
french: C'est amusant ! Merci, [Ari].
russian: Прелестно! Спасибо, [Ari].
bulgarian: How fun! Cheers, [Ari].

english: I enjoy how unsettling mushrooms look, and =Morel Mushrooms= are especially so.
french: J'adore l'aspect dérangeant de certains champignons, et les =morilles= en sont le meilleur exemple.
russian: Грибы мне нравятся своим пугающим видом, особенно =сморчки=.
bulgarian: I enjoy how unsettling mushrooms look, and =Morel Mushrooms= are especially so.

english: The taste isn't for everyone, but that means more for yours truly.
french: Tout le monde n'aime pas le goût, ce qui fait que je n'aurai pas à la partager.
russian: Такой вкус не всем по нраву. Но это лишь значит, что вашей покорной больше достанется.
bulgarian: The taste isn't for everyone, but that means more for yours truly.

english: I love an earthy =Mushroom Brew=. Thank you, [Ari].
french: J'adore l'=infusion de champignons=, c'est très bon pour la santé. Merci, [Ari].
russian: Мне нравится землистость =грибной настойки=. Спасибо, [Ari].
bulgarian: I love an earthy =Mushroom Brew=. Thank you, [Ari].

english: I hope you didn't get stung picking this one.
french: J'espère que tu ne t'es pas fait piquer en ramassant celle-ci.
russian:
Надеюсь, ты не

обожглись

обожгласьобжёгсяобожглось при сборе.
bulgarian: I hope you didn't get stung picking this one.

russian: Знаешь, я в очень раннем возрасте научилась собирать =крапиву=.
bulgarian: You know, I learned to pick =Nettles= when I was very young.

english: Hmm. Thanks.
french: Mmm. Merci.
russian: Хмм. Спасибо.
bulgarian: Hmm. Thanks.

english: Oh, [Ari] you shouldn't have! I can always use a nice fresh =Newt=.
french: Oh, [Ari], il ne fallait pas ! J'ai toujours besoin de =tritons= bien frais.
russian: Ох, [Ari], ты меня балуешь! Свеженький =тритон= мне всегда пригодится.
bulgarian: Oh, [Ari] you shouldn't have! I can always use a nice fresh =Newt=.

english: Oh, you didn't know? Well... no take backs.
french: Oh, tu l'ignorais ? Bon... maintenant que c'est dit...
russian:
Что, ты не

знали

зналазналзнало? Поздно, назад не отдам.
bulgarian: Oh, you didn't know? Well... no take backs.

english: It's interesting isn't it, that flowers like the =Night Queen= have certain magical properties?
french: C'est intéressant de savoir que des fleurs comme la =fleur de lune= ont des propriétés magiques, non ?
russian: Любопытно, что у некоторых цветов есть волшебные свойства. Например, у =царицы ночи=.
bulgarian: It's interesting isn't it, that flowers like the =Night Queen= have certain magical properties?

english: You've done me a service this day, [Ari].

russian:
Ты сегодня мне хорошо

услужили

услужилауслужилуслужило, [Ari].

english: Ah, =Pizza=. Good hot, better cold, truly the perfect food.
french: Ah, de la =pizza=. Elle est bonne chaude, encore meilleure froide, c'est le plat idéal.
russian: А, =пицца=. В горячем виде вкусная, в холодном ещё лучше. Идеальная еда.
bulgarian: Ah, =Pizza=. Good hot, better cold, truly the perfect food.

english: Although they're not as poisonous as one might hope. Ah well.
french: Même si elle n'est pas aussi toxique qu'on pourrait le souhaiter. Rien n'est parfait.
russian: Хотя они и не настолько ядовитые, как хотелось бы. Ну ничего.
bulgarian: Although they're not as poisonous as one might hope. Ah well.

english: Thank you anyway.
french: Merci quand même.
russian: Всё равно спасибо.
bulgarian: Thank you anyway.

english: There's nothing like a nice =Poinsettia= for brightening a room.
french: Rien de tel qu'une =euphorbe= pour égayer une pièce.
russian: =Пуансеттии= замечательно подходят, чтобы добавить света в пространство.
bulgarian: There's nothing like a nice =Poinsettia= for brightening a room.

english: I hope you handled it carefully, they're quite poisonous.

russian:
Надеюсь, ты

несланёснесло его осторожно: он весьма ядовитый.

english: A =Red Toadstool=! Thank you, [Ari].

russian: А, =мухомор=! Спасибо, [Ari].
bulgarian: A =Red Toadstool=! Thank you, [Ari].

english: =Red Wine=? I do like a glass of red.
french: Du =vin rouge= ? J'aime bien boire un verre de temps à autre.
russian: =Красное вино=? Да, не откажусь от бокальчика красного.
bulgarian: =Red Wine=? I do like a glass of red.

english: Thank you, [Ari]. This kind of flower suits me.
french: Merci, [Ari]. Ce genre de fleur me convient tout à fait.
russian: Спасибо, [Ari]. Такой цветок мне подходит.
bulgarian: Thank you, [Ari]. This kind of flower suits me.

english: Ah, =Shadow Flower=.
french: Ah, une =pénombranthe=.
russian: А, =теневой цветок=.
bulgarian: Ah, =Shadow Flower=.

english: Smooth.
french: Pourquoi pas ?!
russian: Очаровательно.
bulgarian: Smooth.

english: You're giving dirt to the owner of the Bathhouse?
french: Tu offres une motte de terre à une femme qui dirige des bains ?
russian: Ты даришь хозяйке купальни землю?
bulgarian: You're giving dirt to the owner of the Bathhouse?

english: Well, I won't pry. Which means you shouldn't ask what spellwork I'll be using this fruit for.
french: Non, ne me dis pas ! En retour, ne me demande pas à quel sort ce fruit me servira.
russian: Ладно, не буду допытываться. А значит, и ты не будешь спрашивать, в какой магии я буду этот плод применять.
bulgarian: Well, I won't pry. Which means you shouldn't ask what spellwork I'll be using this fruit for.

раздобылараздобылраздобыло =волшебный плод=?

russian: Это, конечно, трата ценного ингредиента для моих опытов...

english: So I suppose I'll need to savor it. Thanks, [Ari].

russian: Так что распробую его как следует. Спасибо, [Ari].
bulgarian: So I suppose I'll need to savor it. Thanks, [Ari].

english: A =Spell Fruit Parfait=!

bulgarian: A =Spell Fruit Parfait=!

english: Thanks, [Ari].

russian: Спасибо, [Ari].
bulgarian: Thanks, [Ari].

french: Je...

bulgarian: Oh!

english: W-what is this?

english: =Water Chestnut Fritters=! You have good taste, [Ari].
french: Des =beignets de châtaignes d'eau= ! Tu as bon goût, [Ari].
russian: =Жареные водяные орешки=! У тебя хороший вкус, [Ari].

english: I do like a glass of =White Wine=. And it would be rude to turn you down.

english: I put the $Void Newt$ you gave me into my cauldron for safe keeping, but it seems to have slipped out when I wasn't looking.
